title: Five Children and It
description: Five siblings discover a grumpy ancient sand-fairy that grants one wish each day, and rapidly learn that getting exactly what you ask for can be much more troublesome than getting nothing at all.
catalogueBlurb: Five children, one sand-fairy and a new disastrous wish every day.

text.source: Original Story House retelling based on E. Nesbit's public-domain 1902 novel
text.notes: The underlying 1902 novel is public domain in the UK and United States. This wording is an original child-friendly Unicorn Valley retelling. Dated racial and imperial stereotypes in the original have been rewritten rather than reproduced.

illustrations.source: Original 1902 illustrations by H. R. Millar
illustrations.notes: The selected H. R. Millar source files are identified as public domain on Wikimedia Commons.

rights.curatorNotes: Eleven reader sections follow the original sequence of wishes. The chapter built around outdated racial stereotypes has been recast as a general adventure-game wish while preserving the careless-wish plot function. R6.5-WP19SH1.5.2 adds a separately selectable 13-image generated Modern Illustrations set while preserving H. R. Millar as Classic Illustrations.

illustrations.alt: Cyril, Anthea, Robert and Jane discover the grumpy, furry Psammead emerging from the gravel-pit sand.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: The magically beautified children stand at their own front door while Martha refuses to recognise them and the Lamb looks on.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: The four older children sit amid an enormous glittering heap of old golden guineas while the Psammead retreats into the sand.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: Anthea holds the Lamb protectively while Cyril, Robert and Jane fend off several delighted adults who all want the baby.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: Cyril, Anthea, Robert and Jane fly over the English countryside on enormous feathered wings.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: The four wingless children realise they are stranded high on a church tower at sunset beside a locked door.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: Robert, still in his green clothes, stares as the White House has become a vast medieval castle surrounded by tents and soldiers.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: The four children improvise a defence from the battlements with water, fruit, bedding and a broom while the besieging force gathers below.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: A gigantic Robert in his familiar green clothes towers over Cyril, Anthea and Jane while astonished villagers look on.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: The suddenly grown Lamb, now a slight blond young man in a grey flannel suit, green tie and small moustache, looks baffled as Martha fusses over him.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: The four children cautiously face a coherent band of confused travellers and warriors who have become real rather than remaining characters in their game.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: Mother admires a newly appeared jewel in her bedroom while more jewellery surrounds her and the four children react with horror.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

illustrations.alt: At sunset in the gravel pit, the four children gather quietly around the tired Psammead as it prepares to disappear into the sand.
illustrations.caption: Modern Story House illustration.

text.source: Five Children and It, Project Gutenberg eBook #17314
text.notes: The complete public-domain novel text is retained without abridgement or modernisation. Project Gutenberg boilerplate, page markers, illustration captions and transcriber's notes are excluded. The historical text contains dated racial and imperial stereotypes that the Story House Edition deliberately rewrites.

illustrations.source: Original 1902 illustrations by H. R. Millar
illustrations.notes: Eight previously verified H. R. Millar illustrations are reused beside matching passages in the complete classic text.

edition.notes: Story House pagination changes presentation only; all 11 chapters and the original wording remain complete.

rights.curatorNotes: All 11 chapters are reflowed into 125 reader pages at paragraph boundaries. H. R. Millar remains available as Classic Illustrations. Twelve of the generated R6.5-WP19SH1.5.2 images are available as Modern Illustrations; the rewritten Story House-only Chapter 10 image is intentionally not mapped onto the original classic chapter because the source text contains materially different dated racial content.
